items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names are mostly clear (apiRequestAfterSale, updateAfterSalePreview, refundedQtyBySku) and there are section-banner comments. But the visible business code has short names like `oi`, `ri`, `r`, `inp`, and large template-literal HTML blocks with inline styles hurt scanning.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: One 3,547-line file, so capped at accept. The after-sale refund formula is re-implemented in updateAfterSalePreview (allItemsRefunded, payable/subtotal) instead of reusing the core function. Everything hangs off window.* globals, with lots of inline-styled HTML strings.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Inputs are validated (Number.isInteger qty checks, the import shows 原有数据未受影响). But money uses float round2, magic values are inline (e.g. the 10% member rate, threshold literals), and the preview quietly falls back to ¥0.00 on invalid input.

items.name: Clerk workbench usability: amount breakdown, status hints, dangerous-action confirmation
items.name_zh: 店员工作台可用性：金额明细、状态提示与危险操作确认
items.evidence: There is a clear breakdown (原价/实付/已退/剩余可退), the allocation rule is explained, actions depend on status, toasts give feedback, and restock asks for 二次确认. But submitAfterSaleModal refunds with no confirm, and handleImportFromTextarea overwrites data with no confirm.

items.name: Business logic lives in one place (UI and test API share it; integer-cent money)
items.name_zh: 业务逻辑集中且被界面与测试接口共用（金额按分计算）
items.evidence: The UI calls the same apiRequestAfterSale/apiImportData functions as the test API, and stats are derived from records. However, money is float arithmetic with round2 rather than integer cents, and the refund preview duplicates the allocation logic in the UI.
